newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended a second lacklustre day just weaker on Thursday, weathering blows from losses on Wall Street on overnight and falls on the local rand and bond market.
Dealers said that although trading turnover on the day was above average, with deals worth around 760 million rand taking place, this was boosted by a small number of large transactions.
"There were big blocks of stocks, like bookovers, and the big overnight deal in Iscor. There are not a lot of orders moving through the market," a dealer said.
Some 37 million shares in iron and steel firm Iscor traded in a deal worth over 120 million rand with a foreign partner, dealers said.
The brokerage which executed the deal, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, declined to comment and Iscor said it had no further details on the transaction.
Good two-way trade was also seen in Richemont which upped 50 cents to 57.25 rand and Johnnic which was steady at 59 rand, dealers said.
The 100 percent all-share index finished down only 3.4 points at 7,045.1 after the industrial index slipped 6.2 at 8,243.7.

"With the way the rand weakened this morning, I would have thought that industrials would have been down a lot more. There are really not a lot of sellers around despite the Dow coming off," one dealer said.
The rand touched its weakest level in five weeks on Thursday, sliding to a worst day's position of 4.4735 bid, taking the bond market down with it.
The Dow lost 45 points on Wednesday night.
On the gold board, activity was equally subdued with the index adding 1.9 points to 1,311.1. Amongst metal stocks, Vaal Reefs added 150 cents to 278 rand and Dries upped 50 cents to 43.20 rand.

Stocks' dull performance this week, dampened further on Tuesday and Thursday by cricket matches between South Africa and Australia in Johannesburg, was expected to grip the market again on Friday and may develop into a longer-term trend.

"We see trading remaining low key until interest rates are cut sometime in the second half of the year," Jeremy Bolton, portfolio manager of Old Mutual Investors Fund, which has assets of 5.5 billion rand, said on Thursday.
Equity index futures contracts remained in weaker territory in afternoon trade weighed by the Dow's overnight loss and falls on the rand and bond market.
The June all-share contract was at 6,490/95 from 6,513, the near-month June contract at 8,034/44 from 8,073 and June gold at 920/30 from 919 settlement.
